# MeshWatch

> The Apple Watch + iPhone client for [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) and
> for any machine on your Tailscale mesh. One `meshd` per machine exposes htop-style
> stats, coding-agent sessions and usage limits over HTTP; the phone polls the mesh
> and relays to the watch. Local-first: no cloud service, no account, bearer token
> per machine.

Orca ships desktop, iOS and Android clients but no watchOS app. `meshd` merges
sessions from three sources into one list — rmux/tmux, cmux, and Orca via its `orca`
CLI — so an Orca user gets a watch client without changing anything on their side.
Orca terminals appear as `orca:<handle>` and support read and send; they are closed
from Orca itself.

Two things ship from this repo: the **SwiftUI app** (Xcode project, iPhone relay +
watchOS app, not on the App Store) and the **mesh payload** (`meshd`, `rmux-bridge`,
hook tools, and the `mesh` CLI — bun + TypeScript), which is published as a release
of the public repo LeSearch-AI/mesh-install.

Install a machine into the mesh — this is the whole setup, on macOS, Linux or WSL:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/LeSearch-AI/mesh-install/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

It installs bun if missing, installs into `~/.mesh`, starts `meshd` under launchd
(macOS) or `systemd --user` (Linux), and prints an address and a generated token.
Useful suffixes: `-s -- --upgrade`, `-s -- --token <t>`, `-s -- --only meshd`,
`-s -- --uninstall --purge`.

`mesh` CLI (`~/.mesh/bin/mesh`, config `~/.mesh/hosts.json`, `--json` on every
command for machine-readable output):

```sh
mesh host add <name> <ip> [--port N] [--token T]   # hosts: add / rm / default
mesh hosts                                          # list hosts + reachability
mesh ls            [-H host]                        # sessions (alias: agents)
mesh peek <s>      [-H host] [-n lines] [--pane P]  # recent output
mesh send <s> <text...>                             # type text + Enter
mesh key  <s> <enter|ctrl-c|up|down|tab|escape|...> # single key
mesh new  <name> [--cmd claude|codex|pi|...] [--cwd DIR] [--task "..."]
mesh kill <s>
mesh usage         [-H host]                        # limits (alias: limits)
mesh health                                         # is meshd up?
mesh events        [--since ISO]
mesh help [cmd] | mesh man | mesh version
```

meshd HTTP API — `0.0.0.0:8899`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on everything
except `/health`:

```
GET    /health                       # unauthenticated; ok, host, platform, arch,
                                     # uptimeSec, meshdVersion, capabilities[]
                                     # ("orca" present only when Orca is reachable)
GET    /stats                        # cpu / memory / disk / load / top processes
GET    /tailnet                      # tailscale peers
GET    /agents                       # merged sessions: rmux/tmux + cmux + orca:*
POST   /agents/new                   # {name, cmd?, cwd?, initialText?}
DELETE /agents/:name                 # kill session
GET    /agents/:name/output?lines=&pane=
POST   /agents/:name/send            # {text?, key?, pane?}
GET    /agents/:name/panes
POST   /agents/:name/panes           # {dir?}
DELETE /agents/:name/panes/:pane
GET    /usage                        # OpenUsage limits (macOS)
GET    /screen.jpg                   # screenshot
GET    /events?since=ISO             # agent events (hook notifications)
POST   /events
PUT    /kb   ·  POST /kb             # knowledge base entry
GET    /kb/search?q=&scope=&kind=&limit=&federate=0   # federates across peers
GET    /kb/:scope/:key
```

The source repo (`aryateja2106/lecoder-watch`) is **private**, so the relative paths
below resolve only in a checkout. Everything under an `https://` URL is public.

## Install and distribution

- [Installer README](install/README.md): flags, components, env vars, what lands in `~/.mesh`, hook smoke tests, uninstall.
- [install.sh](install/install.sh): the POSIX-sh installer itself. Payload resolution order: a `payload/` dir beside the script, then `--src`, then `MESH_FALLBACK_SRC` (defaults to the published release).
- [mesh CLI + remote install runbook](docs/mesh-cli-and-remote-install.md): adding a host over SSH, upgrading, the dev/air-gapped serving path.
- [LeSearch-AI/mesh-install](https://github.com/LeSearch-AI/mesh-install): public release-hosting repo. No source; only the assets the one-liner resolves against.
- [install.sh (latest release)](https://github.com/LeSearch-AI/mesh-install/releases/latest/download/install.sh): what the one-liner actually downloads.
- [mesh-install.tgz (latest release)](https://github.com/LeSearch-AI/mesh-install/releases/latest/download/mesh-install.tgz): the payload tarball, layout `install/{install.sh,README.md,hooks/,payload/}`.
- [SHA256SUMS.txt (latest release)](https://github.com/LeSearch-AI/mesh-install/releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS.txt): verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Source

- [README](README.md): what the app does, the architecture diagram, Xcode build commands.
- [meshd/server.ts](install/payload/meshd/server.ts): the daemon — routing table, stats, session merge, usage, events, KB.
- [meshd/orca.ts](install/payload/meshd/orca.ts): the Orca adapter — maps `orca terminal list/read/send` onto meshd's agent shape.
- [bin/mesh](install/payload/bin/mesh): the CLI, dependency-free bun script.
- [mesh(1)](install/payload/share/man/man1/mesh.1): the man page, also readable as `mesh man`.
- [check-orca-adapter.ts](scripts/check-orca-adapter.ts): hermetic self-check that replays captured `orca --json` envelopes; run with `bun scripts/check-orca-adapter.ts`.

## Releasing

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): Keep a Changelog, semver, back to 0.1.0.
- [RELEASING](docs/RELEASING.md): the versioning contract, how to cut a release, how to verify it.
- [release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml): tag `v*` builds and publishes to LeSearch-AI/mesh-install.
- [package-mesh-install.sh](scripts/package-mesh-install.sh): builds the tarball and stamps `install.sh` with its source URL.

## Optional

- [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca): MIT-licensed agent orchestrator. Integration is over its bundled `orca` CLI with `--json`, its documented agent contract — not the `:6768` WebSocket, which is end-to-end encrypted behind an undocumented handshake.
- [Homebrew formula](packaging/homebrew/lesearch-mesh.rb): `mesh` CLI only, not meshd. The tap repo does not exist yet.
- [npm launcher](packaging/npm/package.json): `npx @lesearch/mesh`. Unpublished.
- [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com): how machines reach each other. On one Wi-Fi it can be skipped.
- [bun](https://bun.sh): the only runtime dependency; the installer fetches it when missing.
- [Project state and learnings](docs/PROJECT-STATE-AND-LEARNINGS-2026-07-07.md): design decisions and known device-testing gaps.
